Task: Model seasonal vegetation dynamics
the workflow models seasonal vegetation dynamics using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data over a specified point in California from 2019 to 2020. It computes the Normalized Ratio Vegetation (NRV) index weekly, fits a harmonic regression model to capture phenological patterns, derives the first derivative to detect changes in vegetation growth rates, and identifies peak timing by analyzing second-order change (D2) in the fitted signal. Outputs include a time-series of NRV images, harmonic trend coefficients, and detected peaks (minimum and maximum weeks), enabling analysis of crop phenology such as emergence and senescence timing.

Calculate daily mean land surface temperature (LST) from MODIS MOD11A2 data over a specified region of interest for the year 2019. The final output is a CSV file exported via Drive containing daily mean LST values for the entire period.

Task: Estimate land surface temperature

Monitor changes in vegetation over Mauritius by computing NDVI and EVI2 from Sentinel-2 imagery for two time periods: a baseline (132–106 days before current date) and a recent period (16 days before to current date). It applies cloud masking using the QA60 band, calculates normalized indices, removes local background effects using focal median subtraction, and generates difference composites visualized as RGB stacks. Outputs include true-color and false-color composites from Sentinel-2, Landsat 8, and Sentinel-1, along with ocean temperature (SST) and chlorophyll concentration from GCOM-C, all displayed in a split-panel interface for comparison. The system supports user interaction via a GUI to select AOI and time ranges, and exports processed images to Google Drive.

The output is a flattened feature collection containing mean values per year-variable combination over the AOI, exported as a CSV table.

Task: Detect land cover change using GLAD and Sentinel-2
Monitor land cover changes in Myanmar by analyzing time-series satellite imagery from Landsat 8, Sentinel-2, and Sentinel-1, along with deforestation alerts from GLAD and fire detections from FIRMS. It computes NDVI and EVI2 differences between two periods using normalized composites, applies cloud masking and confidence filtering on fire data, and visualizes change patterns through RGB composites and difference layers. Outputs include median composites for pre- and post-alert periods, vegetation index differences (NDVI/EVI2), GLAD deforestation alerts filtered by date and confidence, FIRMS thermal anomalies with user-defined confidence thresholds, and dual-polarized Sentinel-1 VV/VH intensity and difference maps. All outputs are clipped to user-selected AOIs and exported to Google Drive.

Monitor vegetation changes in Myanmar by comparing NDVI and EVI2 derived from Sentinel-2 imagery before and after a specified alert period. It uses GLAD deforestation alerts and FIRMS active fire data to identify areas of potential disturbance, applies cloud masking and normalization using a focal median filter, and visualizes differences in vegetation indices over time. Task: Classify habitat types using Sentinel-2
Classify habitat types in the Southern Buh region using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from 2019. It divides the year into eight phenological time windows based on Julian day ranges, computes median composites for each period with cloud masking applied, and selects specific spectral bands. A Random Forest classifier is trained using labeled training data (based on EUNIS 2020 classification system) to map habitats. The output includes a classified land cover map, variable importance chart, confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and Kappa statistic, all exported to Google Drive along with the full composite image.

Task: Classify land cover using multi-temporal Sentinel-2 imagery
the workflow performs a land use and land cover (LCLU) classification for Córdoba, Argentina, using multi-temporal Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from July 2020 to April 2021. It computes vegetation and water indices (EVI, MSAVI, MNDWI), applies cloud and shadow masking, and generates a stacked composite image across seven time periods. Training samples are extracted from a stratified sample of 1,000 points based on an initial classification mask (maskloop2). Three classifiers—Random Forest, CART, and SVM—are trained and applied to produce final LCLU maps, which are exported as assets. The output includes classified raster images representing thematic land cover classes such as urban, agriculture, natural vegetation, water, and bare soil.

It first classifies urban and rural areas based on IGBP land cover types from MCD12Q1, then computes mean land surface temperature (LST) for urban and rural zones using daily MODIS LST data (MOD11A1) resampled to 500m. Outputs include a single UHI image (annual average difference) and a multi-band image collection representing monthly UHI intensities.

instruction:
Task: Map flood extent using Sentinel-1 SAR
Map flood extent in Tanggamus Regency, Indonesia, using pre- and post-flood Sentinel-1 GRD (Ground Range Detected) SAR imagery (VH polarization, IW mode, 10 m resolution). It computes a ratio-based change detection (after/before), applies speckle filtering (focal_mean), masks out perennial water bodies using JRC Global Surface Water seasonality layer (≥10 months), removes small noise objects via connected pixel count (≥8), and excludes steep terrain (slope < 5° from HydroSHEDS DEM). Outputs include: (1) a binary flood extent raster and vector (SHP) for QGIS; (2) flood area in hectares; (3) exposed population count (using GHSL 2015 250 m); (4) affected cropland and urban area (using MODIS MCD12Q1 LC_Type1 classes 12/14 and 13); and (5) interactive map visualization with legends and statistics panel.

Task: Compute tasseled cap components
the workflow performs three advanced pixel-based image transformations on Landsat imagery: (1) Tasseled Cap transformation for Landsat 5 using a predefined 6×6 rotation matrix (RT) applied to TOA reflectance bands B1–B7 to derive brightness, greenness, and wetness components; (2) Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on Landsat 8 TOA bands B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B10, B11, computing the covariance matrix, eigenvectors, and projecting the data onto principal components; and (3) Linear spectral unmixing of Landsat 8 bands B2–B7 using endmembers derived from mean reflectance in manually digitized bare soil, water, and vegetation polygons, yielding fractional abundance maps ('bare', 'veg', 'water'). It also demonstrates an HSV color space transformation and pan-sharpening using the panchromatic band (B8). All outputs are visualized as interactive map layers in the GEE Code Editor.
